cards.text: Paul's in Ephesus, where a silversmith named Demetrius just got the whole city worked up over the goddess Artemis, and the city filled with confusion (Acts 19:24-29). Now the uproar is finally over, and Paul's about to head out. But before he goes, he sends for the disciples.

cards.question: Paul sends for the disciples one more time before he leaves. What does he do with them?

answers.text: He scolds them for the riot

cards.text: He says goodbye and leaves for Macedonia, speaking many words of encouragement all through that area. Then he arrives in Greece.

cards.question: Paul stays in Greece for three ___.

cards.text: Paul's about to sail for Syria when some Jews form a plot against him. That's like hearing somebody's waiting for you at the airport, and they did NOT bring a welcome sign.

cards.question: With a plot against him right as he's about to sail for Syria, what does Paul decide to do?

cards.text: Paul's not traveling alone, either. Seven men go with him, and one of them is Timothy, a disciple Paul first took along on his travels back in Acts 16:1-3.
Those men go on ahead and wait in Troas. And catch this: the writer says they waited for "us," so whoever's writing this story is on the trip too.

cards.question: Paul and the writer sail from Philippi to catch up with the others in Troas. After which feast do they set sail?
When Paul and the writer reach Troas, the men who went on ahead are there waiting, and they all join back up.

cards.text: It takes them five days to get there, and they stay in Troas seven days. Then on the first day of the week, everyone comes together to break bread, and Paul starts talking.

cards.question: Paul is ready to leave the next day, so he talks to them and keeps on speaking until ___.

cards.text: There are many lamps in the upper room, and a young man named Eutychus is sitting in the window. Paul talks on and on, and friend, I have seen ovens preheat FASTER than this talk wraps up.

cards.question: As Paul talks on and on, Eutychus sinks into a deep sleep.

cards.text: Friend, I can't judge, because I once fell asleep waiting on a TWELVE-minute batch of cookies. But Eutychus is sound asleep, and then he falls from the third story.

cards.question: When they pick Eutychus up after his fall from the third story, he's shaken up but fine.

cards.text: Eutychus is picked up dead. But Paul goes down, throws himself on the young man and wraps him up in a hug.

cards.question: Paul tells everyone not to be alarmed. He says the young man is still ___.
A young man just fell out of a WINDOW. I'd need a week off. Paul goes back upstairs, breaks bread and eats. Then what does he do?

answers.text: Leaves for the ship right away

cards.text: At daybreak Paul heads out, and the people are greatly relieved to take the boy home alive. Paul's still on the road, friend, and this journey isn't done yet.
